text: On 29 August 2022 Ukraine announced an offensive in Kherson Oblast after weeks of public talk about it.
The rout in Kharkiv Oblast pushed Moscow into partial mobilisation on 21 September 2022.
Ukrainian control of Balakliia was formally established on 10 September 2022.
notes: OUTCOME; conflicts with the 8 Sep retaking date given by ISW

text: All of Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil was retaken by Ukraine by 13 September 2022.
Zelensky said on 13 September 2022 that 8,000 km² had been liberated, as reported via Wikipedia.
A DeepState-derived computation gives 10,902 km² recaptured by Ukraine on all fronts in September 2022.
Ukraine put the area retaken in the whole Kharkiv operation, to October 2022, at about 12,000 km² and over 500 settlements.
Wikipedia, citing CNN, gives 338 Russian vehicles lost in the five days to 11 September 2022.
Oryx's master list is the running count of visually confirmed Russian equipment losses.
Ukrainian losses in the Kharkiv counteroffensive are not published.
Zelensky said Ukraine had taken "several hundred" Russian prisoners by 17 September 2022.
A Ukrainian officer claimed over 1,500 Russians were killed at Lyman.
By late August 2022 Russia had already been moving units south toward Kherson, including artillery of the 1st Guards Tank Army.
With Russian units moved south, the Izium–Balakliia sector was left as an economy-of-force front before the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
The Russian defenders of the Izium–Balakliia sector in early September 2022 were a depleted mix of 11th Army Corps troops, Rosgvardia SOBR units, LNR conscripts and BARS volunteer reservists.
Colonel General Oleksandr Syrskyi pitched the Kharkiv attack as a diversion for the Kherson effort.
Syrskyi's concept for the Kharkiv counteroffensive was a single fast blow north of Balakliia and Izium that bypassed towns and cut roads.
At 03:30 on 6 September 2022, after hours of rocket and artillery fire, the 25th Airborne Brigade advanced about 18 km to the road junction at Volokhiv Yar.
Other Ukrainian brigades, including the 92nd Mechanised Brigade and the 3rd Tank Brigade, encircled Balakliia, which was retaken on 8 September 2022.
The Ukrainian exploitation echelon drove east along the N26 to Shevchenkove and Kupiansk, the rail hub on the Oskil.
The 92nd Mechanised Brigade raised the Ukrainian flag over Kupiansk city hall on 10 September 2022.
Cut off from the north, the Russian Izium grouping fled rather than withdrew in September 2022.
On 10 September 2022 the Russian MoD called the retreat from the Izium–Balakliia area a "regrouping" to Donetsk Oblast.
On 11 September 2022 the Russian MoD showed a map conceding all of Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil.
Ukraine halted the main advance of the Kharkiv counteroffensive on the Oskil around 11–12 September 2022.

text: Velykyi Burluk fell to Ukrainian forces on 10–11 September 2022.
Ukrainian troops reached the Russian state border at Vovchansk and Ternova on 11–12 September 2022.
In the Oskil phase Ukraine won bridgeheads at Borova on 13 September 2022, east Kupiansk on 16 September and Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi on 26 September.
Lyman was liberated by Ukrainian forces on 1 October 2022.
Borova town was taken by Ukrainian forces on 3 October 2022.
After the Kharkiv counteroffensive the new Russian line ran Svatove–Kreminna, along the R66, as of 4 October 2022.
The area Ukraine retook in the Kharkiv counteroffensive is contested; the dossier sets the win band for the push to the Oskil at about 6,000–8,500 km².

In spring 2022 Syrskyi started considering a blow north of Balakliia and Izium that would threaten both with encirclement.
In May 2022 Russia reinforced Kupiansk with 4 BTGs to guard its supply lines from Belgorod.
By early September 2022 Russia held only a 10 km strip along the border north of Kharkiv.

On 24 July 2022 a HIMARS strike killed 12 men of the Russian 336th Marine Brigade in the Balakliia area.
In July 2022 US and UK war-gamers judged a broad Ukrainian southern offensive unworkable, and Ukraine narrowed its Kherson plan.
In summer 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff asked commanders for diversionary options, Syrskyi proposed Kharkiv, and Zelensky approved by mid-August.

text: On 26 August 2022 Lt Gen Roman Berdnikov replaced Lt Gen Andrei Sychevoy as commander of the Russian western grouping, according to GUR.
In late August 2022 elements of the 147th Artillery Regiment (2nd Guards MRD, 1st Guards Tank Army) went to Kherson.
In late August 2022 Syrskyi's brigade commanders rehearsed on a 3D-printed terrain model of occupied Kharkiv Oblast.
In late August 2022 Ukraine moved pontoon bridges to feign a direct attack on Izium.
By 30 August 2022 Russia blew the Siverskyi Donets bridge at Bairak, south of Balakliia.
On 29 August 2022 Ukraine's Southern Command announced the Kherson offensive.
On 30 August 2022 the Russian Balakliia force was at 71% strength; its 2nd assault battalion had 49 of 240 men and the 9th BARS was at 23%.

text: On 3 September 2022 the Ukrainian 103rd TDF Brigade crossed the Siverskyi Donets from Kryva Luka and took Ozerne, east of Sloviansk.
On 5 September 2022 Ukrainian troops were seen in Staryi Karavan, north-east of Sloviansk.
On 5 September 2022 Russia postponed the annexation referendums.
On the night of 5–6 September 2022 hours of Ukrainian M270 and artillery fire hit Russian command posts, ammunition and fuel depots.
At about 03:30 on 6 September 2022 the 25th Airborne Brigade advanced in columns of three IFVs, and by evening reached Volokhiv Yar, about 18 km in.
On 6 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Verbivka, less than 3 km from Balakliia.
On 6 September 2022 Russia demolished bridges east of Balakliia.
On 6 September 2022 Hrakove was outflanked and abandoned by Russian forces by evening.
Between 6 and 8 September 2022 Ukrainian precision strikes destroyed the Russian command centre at Balakliia.
By 7 September 2022 Ukrainian forces had gained at least 20 km and about 400 km², advancing along the E40, N26, T2110/T2210 and R78.
On 7 September 2022 HIMARS struck Izium and Kupiansk.
On 7 September 2022 the 112th and 113th TDF Brigades attacked out of Chuhuiv Raion, at Mykolaiivka and Vasylenkove.
On 7 September 2022 Putin said in Vladivostok: "We have not lost anything".
On 8 September 2022 Ukrainian forces retook Balakliia and raised the flag on the city council.
On 8 September 2022 the Russian MoD claimed a strike on a Ukrainian depot in Balakliia, thereby admitting the town's loss.
On the morning of 8 September 2022 the 80th Air Assault Brigade reached the Oskil at Senkove.
By midday on 8 September 2022 Ukrainian forces reached Shevchenkove.
On 8 September 2022 Ukrainian forces were 15–20 km from Kupiansk.
On 8 September 2022 occupation head Ganchev ordered women and children evacuated from Kupiansk and Izium raions.

ISW estimated on 9 September 2022 that Ukraine had retaken about 2,500 km².

On 9 September 2022 Putin convened the Russian Security Council.

On 10 September 2022 the 25th Airborne Brigade entered Izium ahead of plan as Russian columns fled east.
On 10 September 2022 the Russian MoD announced the "regrouping" of the Izium–Balakliia group to Donetsk Oblast.
On 10 September 2022 Moscow held fireworks for Moscow City Day.
On 10 September 2022 Velykyi Burluk was reportedly taken by Ukrainian forces.
On 10 September 2022 Ukrainian forces reached Lyman's southern outskirts.

On 13 September 2022 a Geran-2 fragment was found at Kupiansk.
By 13 September 2022 all of Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil was retaken by Ukraine.

On 14 September 2022 Zelensky visited Izium and decorated units including the 14th and 92nd Mechanised, 25th Airborne and 80th Air Assault Brigades, the 107th Rocket Artillery Brigade, the artillery brigades and HUR.
On 14 September 2022 Russian S-300 and Buk convoys pulled back toward the border.
On 14 September 2022 LNR units leaving Kharkiv Oblast were sent to Donetsk Oblast.
On 15 September 2022 exhumations started at the Izium mass-grave site at Pishanske cemetery.
On 16 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took all of Kupiansk, including the east bank.
After losing Kupiansk in September 2022, Russia rerouted its logistics via the Valuyki rail line.
On 17 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Shchurove, 6 km south-west of Lyman.
On 17 September 2022 the National Guard reported that Ukrainians had reached the Oskil's left bank.
On 18 September 2022 Ukrainian forces captured the first intact T-90M in Kharkiv Oblast.
On 19 September 2022 Bilohorivka in Luhansk Oblast was confirmed retaken by Ukraine.
On 19 September 2022 Russia claimed to have destroyed a Ukrainian pontoon near Dvorichna.
On 21 September 2022 Putin announced partial mobilisation.
Between 22 and 24 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Yatskivka and Korovii Yar and liberated Horobivka, Petropavlivka (7 km east of Kupiansk), Kucherivka and Podoly.
On 26 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi and Pisky-Radkivski.
On 26 September 2022 elements of the Russian 20th CAA and 144th MRD arrived to defend Lyman and Svatove.
On 28 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Zelena Dolyna, Kolodiazi and Novoselivka and raised the flag over Kivsharivka, threatening the Svatove–Lyman road.
On 29–30 September 2022 Ukrainian forces took Stavky and cut the Drobysheve–Torske road.
On 29–30 September 2022 Russia abandoned Drobysheve and Yampil, leaving one egress road from Lyman, under Ukrainian artillery.
On 30 September 2022 Russia sent the partly mobilised 503rd MRR toward Torske.

Berdnikov was named Western Military District commander, as reported on 3 October 2022.
On 4 October 2022 Ukrainian forces took Bohuslavka and Borivska Andriivka.

On 4 October 2022 the National Guard said Kharkiv Oblast was "completely liberated".

text: By 13 October 2022 502 settlements in Kharkiv Oblast had been liberated, according to the Reintegration Ministry.

The playable area of the Kharkiv counteroffensive chapter runs from about 48.9 to 50.3 N and 36.6 to 38.2 E, from the Chuhuiv–Balakliia start line to the Oskil and Svatove in the east, and from the Belgorod border at Vovchansk to Lyman and Sviatohirsk in the south.
The Siverskyi Donets runs north-west to south-east past Balakliia and Izium to Sviatohirsk and Lyman.
The right bank of the Siverskyi Donets is high, with chalk cliffs at Sviati Hory, while its left bank is low, with swamps, oxbows and pine forest on sandy terraces, as at Lyman and Kreminna.
The Oskil runs north–south through Kupiansk to join the Siverskyi Donets near Izium, with the Oskil Reservoir between them.
Pine massifs line both the Oskil and the Siverskyi Donets.
Bielieskov notes that in September 2022 the Oskil Reservoir covered the Ukrainian flank and ruled out Russian manoeuvre east of Izium.
Novaya Gazeta Europe described the Russian Izium grouping as "stranded between two rivers" once Kupiansk and Kunie were threatened in September 2022.

text: Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi is the rail junction of the Kupiansk area, with lines to Kharkiv, Sviatohirsk and Sievierodonetsk, and via Kupiansk to Stary Oskol in Russia.
The Belgorod–Vovchansk–Kupiansk rail line dates from 1901.
Novaya Gazeta Europe names two rail lines from Kupiansk into Russia, via Vovchansk to Belgorod and via Valuyki, which fed Russian forces at Kharkiv, Sloviansk, Bakhmut and Donetsk in 2022.
After Kupiansk fell in September 2022, Russia had to route its logistics through the Valuyki rail line.
Syniehubov called Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi "one of the biggest logistical railway routes" in Kharkiv Oblast.

cites.quote: one of the biggest logistical railway routes

text: Lyman is a rail hub carrying up to 30% of Donetsk railway cargo.

observations.subject: share of Donetsk railway cargo via Lyman

text: Wikipedia lists Balakliia, Shevchenkove, Kupiansk and Izium as the key logistics nodes Russia had held since spring 2022.
Russian Railway Troops rebuild bridges, for example a pontoon rail bridge at Kupiansk.
Russia blew the Siverskyi Donets bridge at Bairak before 30 August 2022.
On 6 September 2022 Russia blew bridges east of Balakliia and over the Serednia Balakliika.
Ukrainian strikes left the Kupiansk road bridge over the Oskil unusable by 9 September 2022.
Ukrainian crossings east of the Oskil in September 2022 were won by fording and pontoon at Borova, Dvorichna and Kupiansk.
In the south, the 103rd Territorial Defence Brigade crossed the Siverskyi Donets at Kryva Luka on 3 September 2022.
East of Kupiansk the shelterbelt grid runs WNW–ESE and NNE–SSW, with 0.62 km of belt per km² and main belts about 1.1 km apart (measured from OSM).

On 6–11 September 2022 the weather at Balakliia and Kupiansk was dry, with 0.0–0.2 mm of rain a day, lows of 5–11 °C, highs of 15–20 °C and mean cloud cover of 33–77% until it closed in on 10–11 September (ERA5 reanalysis).
On 6 September 2022 sunrise was about 05:55 and sunset about 19:05 local time, so the 03:30 H-hour of the Kharkiv counteroffensive was in darkness.
Rain set in on 12–14 September 2022, with 7–14 mm a day at Kupiansk on 12–13 September and 92–100% cloud (ERA5); this coincided with the Ukrainian halt on the Oskil, though no source links the two.
Around Lyman, 28 September – 3 October 2022 was mild and wet, with highs of 19–24 °C, 10 mm of rain on 28 September, 8.5 mm on 1 October and 13 mm on 2–3 October (ERA5).
Kyiv Post reported Ukrainian units in the Sviati Hory forests advancing "at night, in fog or rain".

cites.quote: at night, in fog or rain

text: Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of the Ukrainian Ground Forces, planned and ran the Kharkiv counteroffensive, with Brig Gen Oleksandr Tarnavsky as his deputy and C-in-C Zaluzhnyi above them.
In the Kharkiv counteroffensive the 25th Airborne Brigade took Volokhiv Yar on day 1 and Izium on 10 September 2022, then moved via Korovii Yar into Lyman from the Drobysheve side.
In the Kharkiv counteroffensive the 92nd Mechanised Brigade advanced from Andriivka to Kupiansk, which it took on 10 September 2022.
The 80th Air Assault Brigade reached the Oskil at Senkove on 8 September 2022, and later fought at Oskil village, Yatskivka, Pisky-Radkivski and Borova.
The 3rd Tank Brigade fought at Nova Husarivka, Bairak, Shchurivka and Balakliia, with elements at Izium per Neil Hauer.
notes: Role rests on Wikipedia citing Hauer; needs primary confirmation (dossier 11)

text: The 14th Mechanised Brigade reached Ternova on the border on 12 September 2022.
The 81st Airmobile Brigade took Bohorodychne by 11–12 September 2022 and Novoselivka near Lyman on 28 September.
The 54th Mechanised Brigade is also listed among the Ukrainian manoeuvre brigades of the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
Wikipedia's 4th Guards Tank Division article cites a Ukrainian 4th Tank Brigade trying to encircle that division outside Izium.
notes: Role rests on Wikipedia citing Hauer/Butusov; needs primary confirmation (dossier 11)

text: The 113th Territorial Defence Brigade operated at Shevchenkove, Velykyi Burluk and the border near Vovchansk.
notes: TDF list sits in a block whose citation is at the end of the Territorial Defence item

text: The 112th Territorial Defence Brigade made a 45 km advance to Vovchansk by 12 September 2022.
The 128th, 124th, 107th, 127th and 111th Territorial Defence Brigades also took part; the 107th's 93rd Battalion was at Velyka Komyshuvakha and the 127th north of Kharkiv.
The battalions of the 103rd Territorial Defence Brigade worked the Siverskyi Donets and Lyman flank from 3 September 2022.

Ukrainian fires in the Kharkiv counteroffensive came from the 26th, 40th, 43rd and 44th Artillery Brigades, the 107th Rocket Artillery Brigade and the 15th Artillery Reconnaissance Brigade, as named by Zelensky on 14 September 2022.
Each attacking Ukrainian brigade had at least eight M777s, some delivered the night before H-hour.
HUR (Main Intelligence Directorate) took part in the Kharkiv counteroffensive, and its Kraken unit is reported as key at Izium.
notes: Kraken's role rests on weak Wikipedia sourcing (dossier 11)

text: Ukrainian special forces in the Kharkiv counteroffensive included the "Bohun" unit, whose press officer was Taras Berezovets.
Military-intelligence and SBU units acted as "raid squads" in the Ukrainian exploitation echelon.
The Kharkiv special-forces detachment of the Azov Regiment took part in the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
The National Guard's 15th Regiment and the volunteer battalion "Slobidska Sich" took part in the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
No total Ukrainian strength for the Kharkiv counteroffensive is published; the Washington Post says "thousands" of soldiers were assembled.
Bielieskov says Ukraine "concentrated everything we could" in the Balakliia–Kupiansk–Izium area.
A typical Ukrainian lead company in the Kharkiv counteroffensive was about 100 men moving in columns of three IFVs.
Ukraine used about 32,500 artillery rounds in the first five days of the Kharkiv counteroffensive, against a feared need of over 100,000.
Lt Gen Andrei Sychevoy commanded the Russian western grouping until 26 August 2022, then Lt Gen Roman Berdnikov.
From about 11 September 2022 Col Gen Alexander Lapin of the Central Military District took over the Russian western grouping.
Western Military District commander Zhuravlyov was replaced by Berdnikov, as reported on 3 October 2022.
The Russian Izium grouping peaked at 24 BTGs, about 18,000 troops, and had at least halved by August 2022.
Syrskyi gives the Russian Izium grouping as about 9,000 troops in about 12 BTGs in August 2022.
Novaya Gazeta Europe estimated "more than 10,000" Russian troops near Izium in 2022.
David Axe estimated the Russian force near Izium at 10,000 troops.
notes: Forbes piece returned 403; cited only via Wikipedia

text: The main Russian formations in the Izium area were elements of the 1st Guards Tank Army, namely the 4th Guards Tank Division (not fully reconstituted) and the 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division, plus the 11th Army Corps and the 64th Motor Rifle Brigade.
The 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division's 1st Motor Rifle Regiment left behind fatigue letters dated 30 August 2022.
The Russian Balakliia force was commanded by Col Ivan Popov of the 11th Army Corps (Baltic Fleet), from a bunker in a vehicle-repair complex.

The Balakliia force comprised the 9th Motor Rifle Regiment at Hrakove, elements of the 336th Marine Brigade, Luhansk conscripts (one corporal was 64, and some carried Mosin rifles) and the 9th BARS brigade.
On 30 August 2022 the Balakliia force was at 71% strength overall; the 2nd assault battalion had 49 of 240 men and the 9th BARS was at 23%.
The Balakliia force's equipment fell from 8 APCs to 3 and from 24 Fagot ATGMs to 4; it had 2 drones left, its only Zoopark counter-battery radar was gone, and two of three jammers were broken.
notes: From captured Russian documents reported by Reuters; dates not given beyond late Aug

text: SOBR and Rosgvardia units held Balakliia and lost it without coordination or adequate artillery support.
Bielieskov describes a single Russian defensive tier north of Balakliia, held mainly by SOBR teams.

The Russian Lyman garrison in late September 2022 comprised BARS-13 and BARS-16 ("Kuban"), DNR and LNR units, the 752nd Motor Rifle Regiment and rear troops of the 20th CAA, and the 3rd Guards Spetsnaz Brigade.
Late Russian reinforcements for Lyman included the partly mobilised 503rd Motor Rifle Regiment (58th CAA) at Torske.
Elements of the 144th Motor Rifle Division reinforced the Russian line on the Oskil and at Svatove in late September 2022.
The Russian force encircled at Lyman was "up to 5,000" strong according to Wikipedia, or about 5,500 according to Berezovets.
The only explicit force-ratio figure for the Kharkiv counteroffensive is occupation head Ganchev's claim of "8 times" Ukrainian superiority, which the dossier calls an interested excuse, not a count.
Bielieskov put Russia at 200,000–250,000 troops in Ukraine on a front of more than 1,300 km in 2022, too few for a tiered defence.
Russia held 25,000 troops (Washington Post) to 25–30,000 (Novaya Gazeta Europe) on the Dnipro right bank in 2022.
On 9 September 2022 the Russian units that had left the Kharkiv front came back as reinforcements by road and by helicopter.
LNR units withdrawn from Kharkiv Oblast were sent to Donetsk Oblast rather than to the Oskil in mid-September 2022.
The LNR 206th Regiment was screening the Valuyki rail line inside Russia in September 2022.
In the weeks before the Kharkiv counteroffensive, HIMARS and M270 hit Russian depots and command posts as far back as Kupiansk and Kivsharivka.
Captured Russian documents from Balakliia record HIMARS strikes on Russian command posts from late July 2022.
On the night of 5–6 September 2022 Ukrainian M270 fire left Russian and proxy units unable to receive orders.
ISW judged that Western systems were "necessary but not sufficient" in the Kharkiv counteroffensive: what made the difference was how they were used inside a well-designed campaign.
After the July 2022 HIMARS strikes, Russia could no longer stockpile shells beside its guns.
US geospatial intelligence returned precise locations for the target types Ukraine requested before the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
Extra drones were issued to the Ukrainian attacking brigades to save ammunition in the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
Zaluzhnyi describes the Kharkiv counteroffensive as a combined-arms breach by tank, mechanised and light motorised units under long-range artillery and MLRS, followed by "mobile raiding groups".
Syrskyi's rule in the Kharkiv counteroffensive was to encircle population centres rather than assault them.
Bielieskov describes the "classical" Ukrainian breakthrough development echelon on wheeled armour, cutting roads rather than taking towns.
Ukrainian special forces and light infantry infiltrated at night around Balakliia ahead of the armour.
Ukraine's public announcement of the Kherson offensive served as deception for the Kharkiv counteroffensive.
Before the Kharkiv counteroffensive Ukraine purged informants in Ukrainian-held Kharkiv Oblast.
Ukraine moved pontoon bridges to suggest a direct assault on Izium.
The Ukrainian side stayed silent at the start of the Kharkiv counteroffensive while Russian milbloggers broke the news first.
Russian counters to the Kharkiv counteroffensive included demolishing bridges and requesting artillery on abandoned posts.
Russia rushed reserves to the Kharkiv front by road and helicopter on 9 September 2022.
The Russian Balakliia force had off-the-shelf Mavic drones with uninstalled software, and its EW sets were out of action.
At Lyman the Russian defenders fought: "all the artillery they had" fell on the 25th Airborne Brigade's company.
A Russian R-330Zh Zhitel EW system was destroyed and a Borisoglebsk-2 captured in Kharkiv Oblast in September 2022.
Ukrainian units reused captured Russian T-72s in September 2022.
Analysts saw captured Russian ammunition as more valuable to Ukraine than the guns, given Ukraine's shortage of Soviet-calibre shells.
On 11 September 2022 Russia struck the Ukrainian power grid with Kalibr missiles in reprisal.
On 13 September 2022 the first Geran-2 (Shahed-136) fragment was recovered at Kupiansk.
A Ukrainian company commander used Starlink in Izium in September 2022.

counter: HIMARS and M270 strikes on command posts and depots
measure: Russian command posts and forward ammunition stockpiles beside the guns
effect: units unable to receive orders; shells no longer stockpiled beside guns
rationale: Pre-H-hour strikes on command posts left Russian units unable to receive orders; after the July HIMARS strikes Russia could no longer stockpile shells beside its guns.

text: Before H-hour at 03:30 on 6 September 2022, the Ukrainian assault troops' rendezvous in quiet farmland felt "off" to them; then came hours of M270 fire on headquarters and depots, and columns of three IFVs rolled out in the dark.

By the evening of 6 September 2022 the Ukrainian lead company reached the ravine town of Volokhiv Yar, where a resident had woken to four Russian tanks outside his house, their crews drinking beer in his gazebo and "talking about where to run".

observations.subject: Russian tanks outside a Volokhiv Yar house

text: Ukrainian precision strikes hit the Russian HQ bunker at Balakliia, and the whole site "erupted in flames"; wounded Russians limped out along the road, with Luhansk conscripts trailing behind the Russian column.
The basement of the Russian Balakliia HQ was left with burned papers and a notebook reading: "If you sit and look at the river for long enough, you will eventually see your enemies floating by".

cites.quote: If you sit and look at the river for long enough, you will eventually see your enemies floating by

text: On 8 September 2022 the Ukrainian flag went up on the Balakliia city council.
In the dash down the N26 to Kupiansk, Shevchenkove was bypassed or taken, Kupiansk was shelled at night, and the Oskil bridge was dropped.
On 10 September 2022 the 92nd Mechanised Brigade's 1st Battalion posed with the flag on the Kupiansk city-hall roof while Russians fled from the east bank.
On day 6 the 25th Airborne Brigade's company was told "we're entering Izium" instead of halting on the ridge north of the city.
notes: Set piece says day 6; c06/0021 says Izium was entered on day 5

text: On entering Izium, Ukrainian troops hit a Z-marked Zhiguli that drove into their checkpoint with an RPG, and found working tanks, guns ready to fire and fuel tankers "filled up to the eyeballs" inside the city.
Konashenkov announced a "three-day operation" to transfer the Izium–Balakliia group to Donetsk Oblast.
notes: Dossier gives only the surname Konashenkov

text: Moscow held City Day fireworks on 10 September 2022 while the Izium–Balakliia group was being withdrawn.
On 11 September 2022 the Russian MoD map gave up Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil.
In the border run, the 112th and 113th Territorial Defence Brigades and the 14th Mechanised Brigade drove north through Velykyi Burluk to Vovchansk and Ternova.
The Belgorod border was closed behind civilians fleeing Kharkiv Oblast into Russia.
At Korovii Yar, the 25th Airborne Brigade's company heading for Lyman was hit by three Russian tanks in a tree line: 5 killed and 12 wounded.
After the Korovii Yar ambush a 25th Airborne Brigade squad leader with a shattered jaw led for four more hours, and the advance turned "tougher and slower".
In the Lyman pocket, Ukrainian jaws closed from Drobysheve and Stavky in the north-west and Yampil in the south-east, leaving one road to Torske and Kreminna under artillery fire.
One night a big Russian column leaving the Lyman pocket was heard and shelled.
On 1 October 2022, the day after the annexation ceremony, a Ukrainian flag went up at the Lyman town sign.
Russia's newest tank, the T-90M, was found intact by Ukrainian forces on 18 September 2022.

In summer 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff asked for diversions to support Kherson, and Syrskyi chose the seam between the Izium stronghold and the Belgorod bases, because the Russians thought "you'd have to be crazy" to strike there.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: RUSI judges Syrskyi's choice of the Kharkiv axis by three factors: Russian weakness there, Izium's role as a springboard for attacks on Donbas, and Russian artillery in range of Kharkiv.
Zelensky approved the Kharkiv plan in mid-August 2022 as "a large swath of territory with minimal resources and losses".

cites.quote: a large swath of territory with minimal resources and losses

text: Ukraine chose bypass and speed over reducing towns in the Kharkiv counteroffensive; Syrskyi said "Everything depended on the first day — how far we could break through."

cites.quote: Everything depended on the first day — how far we could break through.

text: The stated risk of the Kharkiv plan was Russian reserves arriving from across the border and cutting off Ukrainians behind the lines.
Ukraine stripped M777s and drones from hotter sectors to give each attacking brigade at least eight howitzers, with tens of thousands of rounds against a feared need of over 100,000.
RUSI judges that Russia saw the Ukrainian build-up before the Kharkiv counteroffensive but had no forces to respond, so Ukraine surprised it on timing, not intent.
Captured Balakliia papers show Russian officers expected an attack "to take control of Balakliia" from late July 2022.
Russian milbloggers had warned of the Kharkiv attack for days before it began.
Syrskyi says Russian warning information about the Kharkiv attack "didn't reach anyone or it wasn't taken into account".

cites.quote: didn't reach anyone or it wasn't taken into account

text: Around 9–10 September 2022, at battalion level, the Ukrainian plan was changed from halting on a ridge north of Izium to entering the city, once intelligence showed "half the units in Izium… are simply fleeing".

cites.quote: half the units in Izium… are simply fleeing

text: On 9–11 September 2022 Moscow first sent convoys and helicopters to the Kharkiv front, then ordered withdrawal behind the Oskil and called it a regrouping.
ISW judged on 11 September 2022 that Russia lacked the reserves to build an Oskil line, and that prudence demanded pulling forces from other sectors to a line further east.
Instead of pulling forces back, Lapin kept attacking at Bakhmut in September 2022.
Posen argues that Russia had deliberately economised in Kharkiv, may have "chosen to accept the loss", and saved most of its units.
notes: Dossier gives only the surname Posen

text: Ukraine halted the main advance at the Oskil around 11 September 2022.
ISW repeatedly said in September 2022 that Ukraine could cross the Oskil "if they choose", because Russia was too weak to hold the whole river.
Defence Minister Reznikov stressed the need to secure the retaken ground against a Russian counterattack on stretched Ukrainian supply lines.
At the Oskil Ukraine chose local bridgeheads at Borova, Kupiansk and Dvorichna rather than a second leap; the sources found give no fuller account of the Ukrainian reasoning.
After a week in Izium, the 25th Airborne Brigade was redirected south-east to Lyman.
The Ukrainian pincer on Lyman came from Sviatohirsk and the Oskil, and cut the Drobysheve–Torske road rather than storming the town.
ISW assessed that the decision not to reinforce Kupiansk and Lyman was almost certainly Putin's, prioritising Kherson and Zaporizhzhia.
The Kharkiv breakthrough exposed how stretched Russia was, and Russian mobilisation followed on 21 September 2022.
RUSI says Ukraine's 2023 planners believed Russia's Kharkiv collapse came from poor morale, when it really came from a shortage of troops.
For days the Russian MoD did not acknowledge the Kharkiv attack; its only statement was a claimed strike on a "Ukrainian depot" in Balakliia, which admitted the town's loss.
Peskov refused to comment on "the situation around Balakliya" on 9 September 2022.

On 10 September 2022 the Russian MoD said a "three-day operation" had transferred the Izium–Balakliia group to Donetsk Oblast "to bolster efforts" there, with "a powerful fire defeat" inflicted to protect the withdrawal.
ISW said on 10 September 2022: "These Russian statements have no relation to the situation on the ground".

cites.quote: These Russian statements have no relation to the situation on the ground

text: On 13 September 2022 the Kremlin admitted defeat for the first time in the war, deflecting blame from Putin onto advisers and the MoD.
Occupation head Ganchev claimed eightfold Ukrainian superiority and organised the evacuation of about 5,000 civilians to Russia.
Russian sources said the Kharkiv front had been held by lightly armed DNR militia.
The Ukrainian expert Kuzan said the Kharkiv front defenders were Russian professionals.
Novaya Gazeta Europe said the Kharkiv front defenders were mainly National Guard, plus DNR/LNR residents and volunteers.
Some Russian milbloggers said Balakliia was given up "in good order", while others said Ukraine had "completely outplayed" the command.
Kadyrov threatened to go to the Kremlin over the Kharkiv defeat.
Girkin, Kots, Duma deputies and Zyuganov called for mobilisation after the Kharkiv defeat.
After Lyman the Russian MoD called it a withdrawal "to more advantageous positions" to avoid encirclement.
After Lyman, Kadyrov and Prigozhin attacked Lapin, and Kremlin-aligned outlets then cast Lapin as the saviour of the trapped Western Military District units.

The Balakliia papers show Russian units at 20–71% of strength, soldiers asking to be released for "physical and moral fatigue", desertion and a self-inflicted wound, and no ammunition or drone resupply arriving in late August 2022.
In August 2022 Russian units moved from the Izium area to Kherson, thinning the battalions around Izium, according to US intelligence relayed by Syrskyi.
